paragraphs.source_en:
25 ‘Thou art fair, and few are fairer’
[To Sophia]
First published in Rossetti 1870 under the title Lines Written for Miss Sophia Stacey and followed by
the notation Via Val Fonda, Florence, the address of the Palazzo Marini where the Shelleys lodged
from 2 October 1819 to 26 January 1820. The MS from which Rossetti took his text was supplied
by the two sons of the woman to whom the verses are addressed in the 1870 title, though ‘with
the sole reservation to themselves of the exclusive right of setting them to music’. Sophia Stacey
(1791–1874) was twenty-eight years old, just over a year older than S., when in November 1819
she arrived in Florence together with her travelling companion Miss Corbet Parry-Jones. The
two women called on the Shelleys on 10 November, and the following day they took lodgings in
the Palazzo Marini where S., Mary and Claire were staying in the boarding-house kept by Mme
